component_findings.actionability: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Messages normally provide enough precise information to correct the issue without requiring unrelated guesswork; suggested fixes count only when semantically reliable. Evidence basis: Compiled adversarial malformed-source samples (e.g. ADV-22b.swift, containing `1@#$` after a valid integer literal) with swiftc and captured raw stderr diagnostics. | swiftc emits precise line:column source locations, renders the offending source line inline with a caret-style underline pointing at the exact token, and gives a human-readable description of the syntactic expectation violated. | On genuinely malformed input the compiler produces several cascaded diagnostics for the same root cause (each subsequent token misparsed), which is common in recursive-descent/error-recovery parsers; the first diagnostic is however precise and actionable. | Runtime diagnostics for adversarial overflow programs (ADV-01 family: Int64->Int32 narrowing of Int64.max) trap with a fatal error identifying 'Fatal error: Int32(_:) failed: the given Int64 is not representable in the target type' including source file/line when built in debug mode -- giving strong runtime diagnosability for undefined/unsafe conversions instead of silent corruption. | Swift diagnostics are on par with modern LLVM-based diagnostics (similar quality to clang/rustc): source-anchored, colorized in a TTY, and generally single-cause-per-message with occasional cascades on complex expression-level syntax errors. | No warnings-as-errors distinctions or lint-level suggestions ("did you mean") were exercised in this sample set…

component_findings.abstraction_reuse: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Functions, modules/types and generic/polymorphic abstraction support reusable composition across ordinary programs. Evidence basis: Inspected reusable comparison programs under template/programs/swift/micro and adversarial, examined idiomatic feature usage, and compiled representative samples with swiftc to confirm language-level capability. | mb10.swift demonstrates a broad, idiomatic feature set in a single 150-line workload: value-type structs with mutating methods (Lcg), optionals and optional binding (guard let, if let), tuple returns, ArraySlice<UInt8> generic slicing without copies, closures used with ContinuousClock().measure, do/try/catch structured error handling, String interpolation, enums-as-sum-type-free error propagation via Never-returning fail(), and CommandLine.arguments for process args. | Foundation (FileHandle, FileManager, Data) is used as standard-library-adjacent tooling providing buffered byte-level I/O APIs (read(upToCount:), write(contentsOf:)) directly, requiring no external dependency to reach C-like performance-oriented I/O -- indicating strong native expressiveness for systems-level tasks without dropping to unsafe code. | Adversarial programs (ADV-01..26) show Swift's integer-overflow semantics are explicit and safe by default: converting Int64 to Int32 with Int32(a) traps on overflow rather than silently truncating, forcing developers to use Int32(truncatingIfNeeded:) or Int32(exactly:) for defined behavior -- a deliberate safety-oriented expressiveness trade columns for oth…
